source.title: The Rock of Melqart: The Ascendancy, Engineering, and Enduring Sieges of Phoenician Tyre
source.author: MiraVerse Cultural & Historical Research Team

passages.excerpt_summary: Tyre (Phoenician ṣūr) developed as an offshore fortified island complemented by mainland Ushu (Palaetyrus), transcending 14th-century BCE Amarna-era shortages.
Geoarchaeological engineering created northern Sidonian and southern Egyptian harbors with 2.25m header limestone blocks and 1-hectare southern basin.

passages.section_title: The Chemistry and Economics of Tyrian Purple
passages.excerpt_summary: Extracting dibromoindigo from Hexaplex trunculus and Bolinus brandaris required 10,000 snails per gram and 10 days of alkaline heating, leaving 40m shell mounds.

passages.section_title: Hiram I and the Solomonic Alliance
passages.excerpt_summary: King Hiram I built the Temple of Melqart with twin gold/emerald pillars and partnered with Solomon on Ships of Tarshish from Ezion-Geber to Ophir.

passages.section_title: Dynastic Crisis & The Foundation of Carthage
passages.excerpt_summary: Following Pygmalion's murder of Sychaeus, Queen Elissa fled Tyre in 814 BCE to found Carthage (Qart-hadasht) using the Byrsa oxhide diplomacy.

passages.section_title: Assyrian Subjugation & The Vassal Treaty of Esarhaddon
passages.excerpt_summary: The 672 BCE treaty with King Ba'al I stripped Tyre of shipwreck salvage rights and invoked divine curses from Phoenician deities (Melqart, Eshmun, Ba'al-samem).

passages.section_title: The Babylonian Cataclysm: The Thirteen-Year Siege
passages.excerpt_summary: Nebuchadnezzar II destroyed mainland Ushu but stalemated against the island for 13 years (586–573 BCE); Ezekiel recorded Babylonian exhaustion; rule transitioned to shoftim.

passages.section_title: The Persian Era & Salamis Naval Flank
passages.excerpt_summary: Tyre served as the naval core of the Achaemenid fleet, fighting on the right wing at Salamis (480 BCE) under King Mattan IV and later navigating Evagoras's rebellion.

passages.section_title: Alexander the Great: Pretext & The 332 BCE Siege
passages.excerpt_summary: Alexander's demand to sacrifice to Heracles-Melqart inside island Tyre was refused by Azemilcus; envoys were executed; Alexander initiated a 7-month siege.

passages.section_title: The Engineering of the Mole & The Tyrian Fireship
passages.excerpt_summary: Alexander built a 60m-wide mole using Palaetyrus rubble and cedar timbers; Tyrians countered with a sulfur/pitch fireship destroying siege towers before naval blockade.

passages.section_title: Geoarchaeological Legacy: Formation of the Tombolo
passages.excerpt_summary: The 60m mole trapped longshore sediment, accumulating 30 million m³ of sand (30,000–50,000 m³/yr) to form a permanent tombolo and bury the Egyptian harbor beneath Roman baths.

passages.section_title: Hellenistic & Roman Numismatics: The Shekel of Tyre
passages.excerpt_summary: Tyrian silver shekels with Heracles-Melqart and eagle on ship's prow became the Levant standard and the mandated currency for the Jerusalem Temple tax.
